_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Accounting P1 (Financial Accounting), November 2019 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The optional
'information' field (array of lines) carries the INFORMATION block of each main question; it is
attached to the FIRST sub-question of that main question and applies to all of its sub-questions.
The pre-printed ANSWER BOOK (paper1_answer_book.pdf) is tracked beside the paper.
memo_answer reproduces the marking guideline's figures and workings line by line (tick marks
removed; marking notes such as 'one part correct' kept). Unnumbered bullet sub-parts of a
question are kept in one entry with their marks added.
The paper's instruction table: Q1 Accounting Concepts and Accounting Equation 25 marks 20 min; Q2 GAAP
Principles, Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Internal Control 73 marks 58 min; Q3 Accounting
Concepts and Interpretation 27 marks 22 min; Q4 Salaries Journal and Internal Control 25 marks 20
min. A Grade 10 Financial Indicator Formula Sheet is attached to the paper (not transcribed here).
In 1.2.4 the answer book pre-prints part (a) (CRJ: Bank +1 900; Debtors control -1 900); only part
(b) earns marks. 3.2.3 quotes the current ratio as 1,6 : 1 where INFORMATION B gives 1,7 : 1.

questions.text: G. Grey, the owner of LOLO Traders, is concerned about the size of his trading stock deficit. (a) • What are the causes of trading stock deficit? Give TWO points. • Suggest TWO realistic measures in order to control and reduce trading stock deficit. (8) (b) The accountant advised the owner (G. Grey) to cash-in the fixed deposit and use the money to pay off part of the loan. Do you agree with the accountant? Give a reason for your answer. (3)
questions.memo_answer:
(a) Causes (any TWO): shoplifting; employee theft; paperwork error; vendor fraud
Measures (any TWO): adequate record-keeping; separation of duties; establish responsibilities; regular and independent stocktaking; access to stock should be limited; extra safety measures should be put in place for every expensive item
(part-mark for unclear responses)
(b) Yes - the reason to pay off debt early is to save money and stop paying interest; paying a large lump sum toward your balance lowers your overall interest costs and helps build equity.
OR No - returns from a fixed deposit are assured and no risk attached; fixed deposits offer higher interest rates as compared to the savings account; by investing in a fixed deposit you can save more than you do with general investment options.

questions.text: Comment on whether the business was more or less profitable than last year. Quote a financial indicator to substantiate your opinion.
questions.memo_answer:
Financial indicator, figure and trend, explanation: The percentage mark-up achieved decreased from 60% budgeted in 2018 to 50% in 2019. The business has therefore not achieved its profit mark-up. It could be due to one of the following reasons:
• Too much discount was allowed during sales
• Mistakes were made when recording prices, source documents or in the books
• Strong competition caused prices to drop
• Suppliers have increased their prices
(part-mark for unclear responses)

questions.text: Comment on the liquidity of the businesses. Quote TWO financial indicators with figures to substantiate your opinion.

questions.memo_answer:
• Current ratio has declined from 3,5 : 1 to 1,6 : 1
• Acid-test ratio has also decreased from 1,6 : 1 to 0,8 : 1
Generally, the business is able to pay off its immediate debts despite the decline in its liquidity position.

questions.text: Do you think the owner should be satisfied with the return on the average owner's equity? Explain by quoting figures.
questions.topic: Analysis and interpretation: liquidity, solvency and return
questions.memo_answer: No. The percentage returned declined from 34,2% in 2018 to 24,6% in 2019. This indicates that the owner's returns are less compared to the previous year (2018). However, the owner gets reasonably good interest on his investment despite the decline compared to other alternative investments. He will, however, have to decide whether it is worth the risk.

questions.text: In so far as internal control is concerned, what should an effective policy regarding salaries and wages entail? State any TWO points.
questions.memo_answer:
Any TWO relevant internal controls (part-mark correct):
(a) There should be adequate supervision of employees to ensure productivity.
(b) Records should be maintained in respect of each employee regarding hours worked, rate per hour; gross salary/wage as per work; details of deductions and applicable taxes; sick, annual and long-service leave available and taken.
(c) All overtime should be approved by the manager.
(d) Wage/salary sheets should be certified correct by a responsible officer.
(e) All salaries and wages should be paid into a banking account as nominated by the employee.
(f) All queries should be dealt with in a transparent manner and should be properly documented.
